title.value: Build a spending-insights app from bank transactions

introduction.value: Plaid describes a Replit connector that lets non-coders prompt the Replit agent to build an app reading their own bank transactions (vendor post, no named user).

method.value: You set up a Replit account and a Plaid dashboard account, then copy your client ID and secret into Replit, which stores them in a vault. Next you add Plaid as a connector and link your bank, or use sandbox data first. Then you prompt the Replit agent to build a dashboard, summary, or chat interface from the categorized transactions. The post doesn't show the agent's own steps.

outcome.value: The post reports no results from a finished app. It says setup takes about five minutes and lists example questions, such as comparing dining spend month to month. A live build demo was scheduled for May 7.

notes.value: You can prototype with Plaid's sandbox synthetic data before linking a real account, and builders can only access their own financial data.

introduction.en: This is a vendor proposal for a personal finance application, rather than a documented customer deployment.
introduction.zh: 这是供应商提出的个人财务应用方案，尚非有记录的客户上线案例。

method.en: Plaid’s vendor example requires Replit and Plaid accounts, a client ID and secret stored through Replit’s vault, and the Plaid connector.
method.zh: Plaid的供应商示例要求Replit及Plaid账户，将client ID和secret经Replit保管库配置，并启用Plaid连接器。

method.en: The builder connects a personal bank account or sandbox data, then asks Replit Agent for a dashboard, spending summary or chat interface using categorized transactions.
method.zh: 开发者连接本人银行账户或沙箱数据，再让Replit Agent基于分类交易生成看板、消费汇总或聊天界面。

outcome.en: The post offers a roughly five-minute setup estimate and sample spending questions; it does not report a finished application’s results or the agent’s execution trace.
outcome.zh: 文章给出约五分钟设置的说法及消费问题示例，没有完成应用的结果，也未展示agent逐步执行轨迹。

notes.en: A demonstration was scheduled for May 7 in the source’s context. Synthetic Plaid data can precede a real connection; the example concerns the builder’s own financial data.
notes.zh: 在原文语境中演示安排于5月7日；可先用Plaid模拟数据再接真实账户，示例仅针对开发者本人的财务数据。

Build a spending-insights app from bank transactions
Plaid describes a Replit connector that lets non-coders prompt the Replit agent to build an app reading their own bank transactions (vendor post, no named user).
Done with
RA
Replit Agent
What they did
You set up a Replit account and a Plaid dashboard account, then copy your client ID and secret into Replit, which stores them in a vault. Next you add Plaid as a connector and link your bank, or use sandbox data first. Then you prompt the Replit agent to build a dashboard, summary, or chat interface from the categorized transactions. The post doesn't show the agent's own steps.
How it went
The post reports no results from a finished app. It says setup takes about five minutes and lists example questions, such as comparing dining spend month to month. A live build demo was scheduled for May 7.
Worth knowing
You can prototype with Plaid's sandbox synthetic data before linking a real account, and builders can only access their own financial data.
Try it yourself
with
Replit Agent
Copy prompt
Build me a web app that connects to my own bank account through Plaid and reads my recent transactions. It should group spending by [categories, e.g. groceries, dining, subscriptions] and show a monthly chart plus a list of my biggest [number] expenses. Use Plaid sandbox test data first, and stop once the dashboard loads and I can see the chart; ask me before connecting any real account or storing any credentials.
Original source: https://plaid.com/blog/build-personalized-finance-apps-replit-plaid/
